Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajesh Shankar

 For the Petitioner : Mr. Sahil, Advocate
 For the State : Mr. Shivam Anand Pathak, A.C. to S.C.Iii

For Res. No.4 : Mrs. Sweety Topno, Advocate

1 .  The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the respondents to measure the house existing over the land appertaining to Khata no.14, plot no.651, area 0.040 acre, Mouja Pipra, which is being acquired for widening of NH-02 in connection with Land Acquisition Case no.22 of 2012-13 and to pay enhanced compensation for the same.
2.

The main submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner was paid the Sukhdeo Saw @ Sukhdeo Kumar Saw vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101619433/
1 awarded amount of compensation of Rs.70,49,897/- in lieu of acquisition of the land in question as well as house existing over the same on old rate.

entities.text: Sukhdeo Saw @ Sukhdeo Kumar Saw vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner represented the concerned authorities in this regard, but no effective step was taken by them, which has compelled the petitioner to file the present writ petition.

3. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent nos.2 and 3, stating, inter alia, that the awarded amount of compensation of Rs.70,49,897/- for the land in question as well as the house existing over the same has already been paid to the petitioner, however, the house/structure has not yet been demolished by him.

4. Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no.4 submits that the petitioner appears to be aggrieved with the quantum of compensation fixed by the respondent no.3 for the house existing over the land in question and, therefore, he has the efficacious/statutory remedy under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter to be referred as 'the Act, 1956') by preferring an application before the Additional Collector, Hazaribagh- cum-Arbitrator under the Act, 1956.
5. Considering that the petitioner has the efficacious/statutory remedy under Section 3G(5) of the Act, 1956, no writ of mandamus can be issued to the concerned authority.

6. The petitioner is, however, at liberty to take appropriate recourse under Section 3G(5) of the Act,
1956 seeking enhancement of compensation for the house in question.
7. The writ petition is, accordingly, disposed of with the aforesaid liberty.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Sanjay/
